snippet.textDisplay: Why the Big 12 is undervalued as a conference. I believe the BIG12 is the second best conference THIS YEAR ONLY. To start the season they have the second best OOC record. If we take all the pre season rankings and bias out of formulas. The results on the field and the computers would also rank the BIG12 the second best top to bottom. SEC is best not going to argue that. 10-2 sums it up fast. History sums it up so do stats and on field results. Then we have the eye test. The Big 12 has looked better top too bottom in the eye test. Better than 3 of the power 4. If you haven’t watched the Big12 this year move on. You have ZERO reference. TV numbers prove yall don’t watch Big12. Yet you comment on crap you know nothing about. When I watch Oklahoma St play Oregon. I can see Oklahoma state is more physical and wins that game at least 7 out of 10 games. Oklahoma State is the Big 12’s - 7th best team. Looks like Oregon, UCLA, or Indiana will likely be the Big 10s best team by the end of the year on a neutral field. Now to the ACC. I watched Miami the best team in the ACC get pushed around by Notre Dame. The 2-4th best team in the Big12 (BYU) pushed around ND. Without their best player. BYU had a one dimensional offense vs ND. Then I watch the way Utah beats Arkansas back when Arkansas had fight in them. When Arkansas fans had hope, players had hope, confidence and pride. Atfter Utah they were whipped dogs. Like UCLA the years they played Utah to start the season. Like Harbough lead Michigan UCLA Florida… Utah is a season wrecker for teams. (See you in Vegas next year MIAMI) I read all the Miami comments about how Utah is overrated, who have they beat. Funny thing is no small brands ever start the season ranked high. It’s a historic fact. How do you think SOS is made? Pre season rankings closely match brand size historically. Almost every year. Don’t believe me look up brand size rankings then pre season top 25 rankings. Rankings should not exist at all for any purpose until week 9-10. Now back to Utahs only factual reference to Georgia. Arkansas was feeling great to start the season 11th best recruiting class. New coach. Great NFL 1st rounder on D. Then Utah bends them over. If Arkansas had respected Utah. Instead of saying how can a Big 12 team compete with a SEC team, the ego wouldn’t be so frail and destroyed. Georgia got Arkansas after feeling defeated and broken. Utah beat them more convincingly than any team Arkansas has played to this point, Georgia, Tennesse… they all got Arkansas after back to back Utah and Georgia. That’s tough for a young team with a new coach. Arkansas is better than people realize. Are they great, no but they are not the worst team in the nation like people say. They might be better than at least 6 teams in the Big 10 maybe 8 in the ACC. Now Is that a perfect reference. No but it’s all we have as a reference point for Utah and Georgia. I bet if you ask Arkansas fans based on field results who is better Utah or Georgia, if they were truly being honest. I think it would be more difficult decision than the nation would expect. I still think they pick Georgia. I don’t blame them. But it would not be such a guarantee. They would certainly say they have a better chance beating any other team in the SEC other than Georgia. Then we have BYU play ND. I hate HATE BYU, but I’m more afraid of Utah facing BYU in the playoffs than ND, MIAMI, Tennessee, Oregon, Ohio state. Yeah looking at the brand size of those programs is scary. I watched Utah go toe to toe with Oregon, USC, Ohio state. Utah can beat them all if Utah plays a good game. Houston is in literally the biggest recruiting city in the nation and it’s not close. Texas Tech is still one of the most talented teams in the nation and has a record of 20-3. I know what you’re thinking ( “TT lost a playoff game”) guess what so did 10 SEC teams the last 3 years. So Georgia should not have a chance this year?) On to Houston, There are more undiscovered 2-3 star recruits out of the city of Houston in the NFL than most entire states including 1-5 star recruits. So don’t make me laugh when you say they don’t have talent. Also Houston has a great program building hot coach. Arizona is a great team in all 3 phases and has a QB in his senior year with 12,000 passing yards. Ahhh, I can show you many teams that a great QB can make a huge difference. BYU is better than ND. They just are. They manhandled ND in the trenches. Beat them without their best player. You could add another hour to the clock I was confident BYU wins. I think the Big 12 is slightly better than the Big 10 this year top to bottom. Do I expect people that watch one game a week to agree with me. No. Do I expect media to agree with me, no. They are paid by viewers. $ talks. Bigger fan bases have more viewers. More viewers = more money 💰. Would Josh pate agree, not on the air. If we look without the pre season rankings of who is “good”. If we look at on the field results. The Big12 should be at least considered on the same footing as Big 10. 3 teams from the Big 12 should be in the playoffs. ND, top 4 SEC, 3 from Big10, G5, 1 ACC. The SEC is the deepest give them 4. My only fear for 5 with the SEC is all the flaws of the SEC teams. I have a hard time thinking Ole Miss can win 4 playoff games in a row with the worst tackling in the nation statistically. Texas has a QB and coach problem. Six win stark hasn’t really changed. He just has more talent and money. It’s like he gets the least out of his player. Alabama is scary, one week and average another. That’s tough when you have to win 4 playoff games in a row. Same for Tennessee. I do think Bama is the second best SEC team. My eyes tell me if I had to pick a Natty from the SEC not named Georgia. It’s Bama. The way they won this week was impressive. I still think the coach hire was a great hire. UCLA has been consistent. I want to see how they do in the CCG. Before I judge them. Utah manhandled them last year. 42-10 I don’t think the teams are all that different from last year. I think the Big 10 is just down and having bad luck with injuries. Investing big money in players that don’t pan out or stay. Oregon lost their depth before this season and it shows. I love Oregon as an Utah fan. I miss being in a conference with them. Ohio state is just unlucky, ego, injury has destroyed them this team this year. Indiana is probably the best team in the Big 10. But they are in a rebuilding year. They lost a ton and don’t have the money like Ohio State, Oregon, USC to just buy a ship. Their ships need building for one more year. Indiana will be legit again next year, mark my words.

snippet.textDisplay:
@nismo-i3e NCAA is not NFL. That’s 64 P4 teams to 32 NFL teams, where 11 P4 (1 G6 team) have a playoff and 7 teams from each conference have a playoff in NFL. That’s over 40% of NFL in playoffs to about 17% of P4 teams in playoffs. According to your comparison of NFL to NCAA, outside of conference champions (divisional in NFL), the rest should be dependent upon record, not an assumed strength of opponent where a horrible loss (2 for TX this year) holds less repercussions than a win against a team with a smaller number determined by corporate media put in front of a name holds merit. It’s either that or assumptions should outweigh record because there was a season where a .500 team beat an undefeated team in the playoffs. How many people really thought a .500 team in NFL was going to go to the Super Bowl, let alone win it? It’s like a double-digit seed winning March Madness.

Do you truly think those corporations care more about determining a correct ranking than making money off the teams they have a contract with? Do you think that they have zero encouragement on the pollsters they have contact and even business affiliation with? ESPN by far has the highest revenue. Where do they make their money in NCAA football?

Since a 12-team playoff, SEC has gone into post season with more opportunity given and has underperformed in playoffs and bowl games. Did it just completely change in the offseason where 1/2 of the SEC is immensely better than the top 1/4 or less than any other conference? Maybe but unlikely.

Because of a few games at the beginning of the year (minimal tape) between P4 conferences as well as media rankings, SEC has been assumed this insanely deep conference of top-tier teams where a loss in the SEC holds more merit than a win in another conference. There’s minimal consideration given to development and zero respect for the quality of a coaching staff because rankings are determined by the opinions of influenced media. 

I’m not saying that Georgia isn’t the best team in the country this year because the SEC hasn’t been able to win the national championship the past few years and because they had a loss to a bad Auburn team. What I’m saying is that a 10-2 team in a P4 conference should be in before a 9-3 team in a P4 conference. The opportunity should be provided to the better record before an assumed by influence better team.

snippet.textDisplay:
@BlakeRamone-c1t Since Lester took over in the 2024-2025 season, Iowa has been averaging about 30 pts a game. After losing about 18 player in the offseason - #1 OL and a top tier DL - they’re a young, inexperienced team, but development has been notable. It’ll likely be like last year where they go to a bowl game and beat another SEC team whining that they didn’t make the playoffs. I hope the OC’s first QB recruit is ready to go next year. Sucks relying on an NIL QB when you don’t have the funds of those blue blood teams. 

TBH, I’m pretty tired of this claim of SEC being so deep because they’re beating the crap out of each other, while B1G is so bad for the same reason. It’s all assumptions based on a few early season games and influenced media opinions. What media corporation has the most revenue, and who’s most beneficial for them to encourage in the rankings? ESPN by far, and to think they don’t use influence to make more is like thinking large corporations don’t use influence on political decisions to profit themselves. I’ll believe the hype when it’s proven in the playoffs and bowl games, but it’s only been hype the past few years. Really seems the mid teams are just getting more competitive by knowing how to use NIL best with their programs. There’s some really good younger coaches out there too that those blue bloods will likely be trying to buy after a few seasons of playoff flops. A 9-3 team in one conference would still likely be 9-3 in another. TX would still have flopped to 2 much lesser teams in B1G, and Indiana would still have found ways to squeak out wins in the SEC. How many 60+ yd FG’s have been made in the SEC this season?
